title: Spatial leakage test: how should we split the data?
text:
Nearby wells have similar nitrate levels. If a test well has close neighbors in the training data, we risk data leakage and overstating the predictive power of our model.
We use the approach found in Estimation of aquifer scale proportion using equal area grids: Assessment of regional scale groundwater quality to divide our map into a square grid. We then perform group k-fold splits, keeping each grid cell intact in the splitting. We evaluate the data leakage by comparing a k-nearest-neighbors model to one that outputs the training mean. Data leakage is measured by comparing the RMSE of the KNN model to that of the mean.

def folds_from(splitter, groups=None):
    """Turn a scikit-learn splitter into one fold number per row."""
    folds = np.empty(len(df), dtype=int)
    for k, (_, test) in enumerate(splitter.split(df, groups=groups)):
        folds[test] = k
    return folds

schemes = {
    "random rows": folds_from(KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=0)),
    "grouped by well": folds_from(GroupKFold(5), groups=df["gm_well_id"]),
}
for km in [1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40]:
    cells = splits.assign_grid_cells(df, cell_size_m=km * 1000)["cell"]
    schemes[f"{km} km blocks"] = splits.spatial_folds(cells, exceeds)
Here, “estimated leakage” is defined as \(1 - \frac{\mathrm{RMSE}_{\mathrm{KNN}}}{\mathrm{RMSE}_\mathrm{mean}}\), where \(\mathrm{RMSE}_{\mathrm{KNN}}\) is the root mean squared error of the K-nearest-neighbors estimator and \(\mathrm{RMSE}_{\mathrm{mean}}\) is the root mean squared error of predicting the mean. If the KNN estimator performs similarly to predicting the mean, then the estimated leakage should be approximately 0; positive values indicate that KNN is performing better. We will graph this below.

section: Problem: original folds were unbalanced by subbasin
text:
Problem: original folds were unbalanced by subbasin
The 10km split balanced the share of samples above 10 mg/L in each fold, but not where the samples came from. Nitrate levels differ strongly between subbasins of the Salinas Valley, so a fold dominated by one subbasin is tested on a region that is underrepresented in its training data. This issue arose in our initial modeling experiments.

def test_distances(data):
    """Distance (m) from each development sample to the nearest well in its training folds."""
    dev = data[~data["holdout"]].reset_index(drop=True)
    xy = leakage.projected_xy(dev, "gm_latitude", "gm_longitude")
    nearest_m = np.full(len(dev), np.nan)
    for train, test in splits.iter_folds(dev["fold"]):
        nearest_m[test] = leakage.nearest_training_distance(xy, train, test)
    return nearest_m


def distance_bands(distances_m):
    """Median distance (km) and the share of samples in each distance band."""
    bands = pd.Series(pd.cut(distances_m, bins=leakage.DISTANCE_BINS, labels=leakage.DISTANCE_LABELS, right=False))
    return pd.concat([pd.Series({"median_km": np.median(distances_m) / 1000}), bands.value_counts(normalize=True, sort=False)])

Findings
In early modeling experiments, model scores varied widely from fold to fold under the original 10km split, and every linear model did worse than predicting the mean on at least one fold. Models performed worst on folds dominated by a subbasin that was underrepresented in training. Stratifying the folds by both subbasin and exceedance roughly halved the fold-to-fold standard deviation of R^2 for every model, and no model scored below the mean on any fold.
We therefore expect predictions to be most reliable within subbasins that already have monitoring wells. This aligns with our goal of identifying where additional nitrate monitoring is most needed in the Salinas Valley. Note that the model has not been tested outside the valley and should not be assumed to transfer to other regions.
Notable finds: - There is a trade-off with balancing subbasins and balancing exceedance. The original 10km split balanced exceedance best (spread 0.020) but subbasins worst (max deviation 0.238). - Smaller cells balance subbasins better (max deviation 0.062 for the 5km grid versus 0.201 for 10km grid), but put test wells closer to training wells (median distance to nearest training well 1.6km and 2.6km respectively for the 5km and 10km grids). - Estimated leakage is close to zero for all four splits (-0.013 to -0.023).
Final decision: the 10km subbasin-stratified split. It reduces the fold-to-fold instability found in the original split while still keeping test wells far from training wells. The location-only leakage test did not detect leakage at 5km, but it is a simple test so we preferred a more conservative split. We also report the originak 10km split as a stress test for predicting in regions that are underrepresented in training.

def plot_fold_map(ax, data, split):
    """Grid cells shaded by fold, wells as dots, with subbasin outlines, for one registered split."""
    size = SPLITS[split]["cell_size_m"]
    holdout = SPLITS[split]["n_splits"] - 1
    wells = data.drop_duplicates("gm_well_id")

    cells = wells.drop_duplicates("cell")[["cell", "fold"]]
    corners = cells["cell"].str.split("_", expand=True).astype(int)     # cell "x_y" -> grid indices
    squares = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
        cells, crs=splits.EQUAL_AREA_CRS,
        geometry=[box(i * size, j * size, (i + 1) * size, (j + 1) * size) for i, j in corners.itertuples(index=False)])
    points = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
        wells, crs="EPSG:4326",
        geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(wells["gm_longitude"], wells["gm_latitude"])).to_crs(splits.EQUAL_AREA_CRS)

    for k, color in enumerate(fold_colors):
        squares[squares["fold"] == k].plot(ax=ax, color=color, alpha=0.25, edgecolor=color, linewidth=0.5)
        label = f"fold {k}" + (" (hold-out)" if k == holdout else "")
        points[points["fold"] == k].plot(ax=ax, color=color, markersize=4, label=label)
    subbasins_ea.boundary.plot(ax=ax, color="black", linewidth=0.6)
    boundary_ea.boundary.plot(ax=ax, color="#52514e", linewidth=1)
    ax.set_title(f"{split}: {size / 1000:g} km cells, stratified by "
                 f"{SPLITS[split]['stratify'].replace('_x_', ' × ')}", loc="left", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_axis_off()

title: Groundwater Feature Integration — Historical Crops (Lag-1)
text:
Objective: Combine groundwater nitrate measurements with soil, terrain, climate, and historical agricultural features into a single table for machine learning.
Procedure - The cleaned groundwater dataset is the starting point: 5,280 nitrate measurements from 1,993 wells sampled 2022–2025 (notebooks/data_cleaning/groundwater/gwater_clean.ipynb). - Soil (SSURGO) and terrain (10 m DEM) features are static and joined by well ID. - PRISM climate features are matched to each sample, using only complete months before the sample date. - Historical crop features (DWR crop maps, 500 m and 1,000 m buffers) are joined by well ID and the year before each nitrate measurement (lag-1; e.g., nitrate from 2023 uses the 2022 crop map). - All joins are left joins that preserve every groundwater observation, and each join is checked for duplicated or unmatched rows.
Output: notebooks/merge/groundwater_ml_integration_lag1_2021_2024_with_climate.csv (5,280 rows × 147 columns), read by src/features/preprocessing.py (load_model_data()).
Local-only inputs (not tracked by Git; place them at these paths): data/soils/soils_huc8_attributes.gpkg and data/elevation/dem_watershed_10m.tif.

METRIC_CRS = "EPSG:3310"

def checked_left_merge(base, features, key, feature_name):
    """Left-join features while preserving the base rows and their order."""
    if key not in base.columns or key not in features.columns:
        raise KeyError(f"{feature_name}: missing join key {key!r}.")
    if features[key].duplicated().any():
        raise ValueError(f"{feature_name}: feature keys are not unique.")

    original_ids = base["observation_id"].copy()
    original_rows = len(base)
    merged = base.merge(
        features,
        on=key,
        how="left",
        validate="many_to_one",
        sort=False,
        indicator="_feature_match",
    )
    if len(merged) != original_rows or not merged["observation_id"].equals(original_ids):
        raise AssertionError(f"{feature_name}: merge changed base rows or order.")

    matched = int(merged["_feature_match"].eq("both").sum())
    coverage = {
        "feature": feature_name,
        "matched_rows": matched,
        "unmatched_rows": original_rows - matched,
        "missing_fraction": (original_rows - matched) / original_rows,
    }
    return merged.drop(columns="_feature_match"), coverage

text:
1. Check the inputs
The checks stop if a required file or column is missing. That keeps an unavailable feature from being silently skipped.


Code
required_paths = [NITRATE_PATH, BUFFER_PATH, SOIL_PATH, DEM_PATH, PRISM_PATH, CROP_PATH]
missing_paths = [path for path in required_paths if not path.exists()]
if missing_paths:
    raise FileNotFoundError("Missing inputs:\n" + "\n".join(map(str, missing_paths)))

observations = pd.read_csv(
    NITRATE_PATH,
    dtype={"gm_well_id": "string", "src_samp_collection_time": "string"},
    parse_dates=["gm_samp_collection_date"],
)
required = {"gm_well_id", "gm_samp_collection_date", "nitrate_mg_L", "gm_latitude", "gm_longitude"}
if not required.issubset(observations.columns):
    raise ValueError(f"Missing nitrate columns: {required - set(observations.columns)}")
if observations.empty:
    raise ValueError("The nitrate table is empty.")
sample_years = observations["gm_samp_collection_date"].dt.year
if not sample_years.between(2022, 2025).all():
    raise ValueError("Expected Charlsey's filtered nitrate data from 2022 through 2025.")
expected_rows = len(observations)
if observations[["gm_well_id", "gm_samp_collection_date"]].isna().any().any():
    raise ValueError("The nitrate table has a missing well ID or sample date.")

observations = observations.copy()
# The canonical CSV row number distinguishes repeated measurements.
observations["source_csv_row"] = observations.index + 2
observations["observation_id"] = "GW-CSV-" + observations["source_csv_row"].astype(str).str.zfill(5)
if observations["observation_id"].duplicated().any():
    raise ValueError("Observation IDs must be unique.")
base_ids = observations["observation_id"].copy()
print("Nitrate rows:", len(observations))

title: Groundwater Feature Integration — Historical Crops (Lag-1)
text:
2. Area-weighted SSURGO features
Existing 500 m buffers are overlaid with SSURGO polygons. Numeric values are averaged by intersected area. Category percentages use mapped category area; coverage percentages show how much of the full buffer is mapped. An absent category is 0 when category data are mapped, while no category coverage remains missing. No minimum coverage cutoff is assumed.


Code
import shapely
buffers = gpd.read_file(BUFFER_PATH)
soils = gpd.read_file(SOIL_PATH)

if buffers.crs is None or soils.crs is None:
    raise ValueError("Both buffer and soil layers need a CRS.")
if buffers.empty:
    raise ValueError("The well buffer layer is empty.")
if buffers.gm_well_id.duplicated().any():
    raise ValueError("Expected one existing buffer per well ID.")

# Check geometries before reprojection or spatial operations. Invalid
# geometries are reported rather than silently repaired.
def check_geometries(frame, layer_name, id_column=None):
    missing = frame.geometry.isna()
    empty = frame.geometry.is_empty
    invalid = ~frame.geometry.is_valid
    problem = missing | empty | invalid

    if problem.any():
        examples = frame.loc[problem, id_column].head(10).tolist() if id_column else frame.index[problem].tolist()[:10]
        raise ValueError(
            f"{layer_name} has {int(problem.sum())} missing, empty, or invalid "
            f"geometries. Examples: {examples}"
        )

    print(f"{layer_name}: all {len(frame)} geometries are valid.")

check_geometries(buffers, "Buffers", "gm_well_id")
check_geometries(soils, "SSURGO soils")

soil_columns = ["slopegradwta", "brockdepmin", "aws0150wta", "drclassdcd", "hydgrpdcd"]
if not set(soil_columns).issubset(soils.columns):
    raise ValueError(f"Missing soil columns: {set(soil_columns) - set(soils.columns)}")

category_fields = ["drclassdcd", "hydgrpdcd"]
category_values = {}
for name in category_fields:
    category_values[name] = sorted(soils[name].dropna().unique(), key=str)

# Area calculations use the same metric CRS for both layers.
buffers = buffers.to_crs("EPSG:3310")
soils = soils.to_crs("EPSG:3310").reset_index(drop=True)

numeric_fields = ["slopegradwta", "brockdepmin", "aws0150wta"]
for name in numeric_fields:
    soils[name] = pd.to_numeric(soils[name], errors="coerce")

soil_features_by_batch = []
batch_size = 100
total_buffers = len(buffers)

for batch_start in range(0, total_buffers, batch_size):
    batch_end = min(batch_start + batch_size, total_buffers)
    batch = buffers.iloc[batch_start:batch_end][["gm_well_id", "geometry"]]

    # Find only soil polygons touching each buffer, then intersect all pairs
    # in one vectorized Shapely operation for this batch.
    candidates = gpd.sjoin(
        batch,
        soils[soil_columns + ["geometry"]],
        how="inner",
        predicate="intersects",
    )

    if candidates.empty:
        pairs = candidates.copy()
        pairs["_intersection_area"] = pd.Series(dtype="float64")
    else:
        soil_positions = candidates["index_right"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
        intersection_geometries = shapely.intersection(
            candidates.geometry.array,
            soils.geometry.array.take(soil_positions),
        )
        intersection_areas = shapely.area(intersection_geometries)
        keep = np.isfinite(intersection_areas) & (intersection_areas > 0)

        pairs = candidates.loc[keep].copy()
        pairs["_intersection_area"] = intersection_areas[keep]

    feature_batch = pd.DataFrame({"gm_well_id": batch["gm_well_id"].to_numpy()})
    buffer_areas = pd.Series(
        batch.geometry.area.to_numpy(),
        index=batch["gm_well_id"].to_numpy(),
    )

    mapped_area = pairs.groupby("gm_well_id")["_intersection_area"].sum()
    mapped_area_for_wells = feature_batch.gm_well_id.map(mapped_area).fillna(0.0)
    if (mapped_area_for_wells.to_numpy() > buffer_areas.to_numpy() * 1.01).any():
        raise ValueError("SSURGO polygons overlap within at least one well buffer.")
    feature_batch["soil_mapped_coverage_pct"] = (
        100 * mapped_area_for_wells.to_numpy() / buffer_areas.to_numpy()
    )

    for name in numeric_fields:
        valid_pairs = pairs.loc[
            pairs[name].notna(), ["gm_well_id", name, "_intersection_area"]
        ]
        valid_area = valid_pairs.groupby("gm_well_id")["_intersection_area"].sum()
        weighted_sum = (
            valid_pairs[name] * valid_pairs["_intersection_area"]
        ).groupby(valid_pairs["gm_well_id"]).sum()

        feature_batch[f"soil_{name}"] = (
            feature_batch.gm_well_id.map(weighted_sum / valid_area).to_numpy()
        )
        feature_batch[f"soil_{name}_coverage_pct"] = (
            100
            * feature_batch.gm_well_id.map(valid_area).fillna(0.0).to_numpy()
            / buffer_areas.to_numpy()
        )

    for name in category_fields:
        valid_pairs = pairs.dropna(subset=[name])
        valid_area = valid_pairs.groupby("gm_well_id")["_intersection_area"].sum()
        valid_area_for_wells = feature_batch.gm_well_id.map(valid_area)

        feature_batch[f"soil_{name}_coverage_pct"] = (
            100
            * valid_area_for_wells.fillna(0.0).to_numpy()
            / buffer_areas.to_numpy()
        )

        category_area = valid_pairs.groupby(
            ["gm_well_id", name], observed=True
        )["_intersection_area"].sum()

        for category in category_values[name]:
            label = str(category).strip().lower().replace(" ", "_").replace("/", "_")
            try:
                area_for_category = category_area.xs(category, level=name)
            except KeyError:
                area_for_category = pd.Series(dtype="float64")

            area_by_well = feature_batch.gm_well_id.map(area_for_category).fillna(0.0)
            percentage = 100 * area_by_well / valid_area_for_wells
            feature_batch[f"soil_{name}_pct_{label}"] = percentage.where(
                valid_area_for_wells > 0
            ).to_numpy()

    soil_features_by_batch.append(feature_batch)
    print(f"Processed SSURGO buffers {batch_start + 1}-{batch_end} of {total_buffers}")

    del candidates, pairs
    if "intersection_geometries" in locals():
        del intersection_geometries
    import gc
    gc.collect()

soil_features = pd.concat(soil_features_by_batch, ignore_index=True)
if soil_features.gm_well_id.duplicated().any():
    raise ValueError("SSURGO feature table is not unique by well.")

print("SSURGO feature rows:", len(soil_features))
print("Average mapped buffer coverage (%):", soil_features.soil_mapped_coverage_pct.mean().round(1))

title: Groundwater Feature Integration — Historical Crops (Lag-1)
text:
3. Terrain features
Elevation is sampled from the 10 m DEM at each well. Topographic position is the well elevation minus the mean valid elevation within the existing 500 m buffer. The DEM CRS is EPSG:4269 (pixel spacing ≈ 0.0000926°, nominally 10 m; exact ground resolution varies with latitude); buffers and distances use EPSG:3310 metres.
Distance to the nearest large river was planned but excluded: the available NHD stream-order values are all missing, so the stream order > 3 filter cannot be applied.


Code
coordinates = observations[["gm_well_id", "gm_longitude", "gm_latitude"]].drop_duplicates()
if coordinates.gm_well_id.duplicated().any():
    raise ValueError("A well ID has conflicting coordinates.")
well_points = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    coordinates,
    geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(coordinates.gm_longitude, coordinates.gm_latitude),
    crs="EPSG:4326",
).to_crs(METRIC_CRS)
buffer_geometry = buffers.set_index("gm_well_id").geometry

dem_features = []
with rasterio.open(DEM_PATH) as dem:
    print("DEM CRS:", dem.crs, "pixel size:", dem.res, "NoData:", dem.nodata)
    points_dem = well_points.to_crs(dem.crs)
    point_values = [np.ma.asarray(next(dem.sample([(p.x, p.y)], masked=True))[0]).filled(np.nan) for p in points_dem.geometry]
    for well_id, point_value in zip(well_points.gm_well_id, point_values):
        polygon = gpd.GeoSeries([buffer_geometry.loc[well_id]], crs=METRIC_CRS).to_crs(dem.crs).iloc[0]
        pixels, _ = mask(dem, [mapping(polygon)], crop=True, filled=False)
        valid = pixels[0].compressed()
        valid = valid[np.isfinite(valid)]
        point_value = float(point_value) if np.isfinite(point_value) else np.nan
        mean_nearby = float(valid.mean()) if len(valid) else np.nan
        dem_features.append({"gm_well_id": well_id, "elevation_m": point_value,
                             "topographic_position": point_value - mean_nearby})
dem_features = pd.DataFrame(dem_features)

title: Groundwater Feature Integration — Historical Crops (Lag-1)
text:
4. Date-safe PRISM climate features
A well is assigned to its nearest PRISM grid point in EPSG:3310. Features use only complete months before the nitrate sample month. Historical means use complete calendar years before the sample year. Inches are converted to millimetres; °F is converted to °C. Earlier nitrate samples may lack PRISM history because this source begins in 2013.


Code
climate = pd.read_csv(PRISM_PATH, parse_dates=["date"])
needed = {"point_id", "longitude", "latitude", "date", "precip_in", "tmean_f"}
if not needed.issubset(climate.columns):
    raise ValueError(f"Missing PRISM columns: {needed - set(climate.columns)}")
if climate.duplicated(["point_id", "date"]).any():
    raise ValueError("Duplicate PRISM point-month records found.")
climate["precip_mm"] = climate.precip_in * 25.4
climate["tmean_c"] = (climate.tmean_f - 32) * 5 / 9
climate["year"] = climate.date.dt.year
climate["month"] = climate.date.dt.month
grid = climate[["point_id", "longitude", "latitude"]].drop_duplicates()
grid = gpd.GeoDataFrame(grid, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(grid.longitude, grid.latitude), crs="EPSG:4326").to_crs(METRIC_CRS)
grid_match = gpd.sjoin_nearest(well_points[["gm_well_id", "geometry"]], grid[["point_id", "geometry"]],
                               how="left", distance_col="prism_grid_distance_m")
grid_match = grid_match.sort_values(["gm_well_id", "prism_grid_distance_m", "point_id"]).drop_duplicates("gm_well_id")
point_for_well = grid_match.set_index("gm_well_id").point_id
by_point = {key: group.sort_values("date").copy() for key, group in climate.groupby("point_id")}

def climate_for_date(point_id, sample_date):
    result = {
        "historical_mean_annual_precip_mm": np.nan,
        "previous_3_complete_months_precip_mm": np.nan,
        "previous_12_complete_months_precip_mm": np.nan,
        "historical_mean_temperature_c": np.nan,
        "previous_3_complete_months_temperature_c": np.nan,
        "previous_12_complete_months_temperature_c": np.nan,
    }
    point_data = by_point.get(point_id)
    if point_data is None:
        return result
    sample_month = sample_date.to_period("M")
    prior = point_data.loc[point_data.date.dt.to_period("M") < sample_month].copy()
    prior["period"] = prior.date.dt.to_period("M")
    for window in [3, 12]:
        periods = pd.period_range(end=sample_month - 1, periods=window, freq="M")
        values = prior.set_index("period").reindex(periods)
        if values.date.notna().all():
            result[f"previous_{window}_complete_months_precip_mm"] = values.precip_mm.sum()
            result[f"previous_{window}_complete_months_temperature_c"] = values.tmean_c.mean()
    prior["year"] = prior.date.dt.year
    full_years = prior.groupby("year").month.nunique()
    full_years = full_years[full_years == 12].index
    history = prior[prior.year.isin(full_years)]
    if not history.empty:
        result["historical_mean_annual_precip_mm"] = history.groupby("year").precip_mm.sum().mean()
        result["historical_mean_temperature_c"] = history.tmean_c.mean()
    return result

climate_rows = []
for row in observations[["gm_well_id", "gm_samp_collection_date"]].itertuples(index=False):
    climate_rows.append(climate_for_date(point_for_well.get(row.gm_well_id),
                                         row.gm_samp_collection_date))
climate_features = pd.DataFrame(climate_rows)
climate_features.insert(0, "observation_id", observations.observation_id.to_numpy())
print("Climate feature missingness:")
display(climate_features.isna().mean().to_frame("missing_fraction"))

text:
5. Historical Crop Features — Lag-1 Integration
Objective: Integrate historical agricultural predictors using the crop map from the year preceding each groundwater nitrate observation.
The crop dataset contains one row per well and crop reference year. Features use consistent 500 m and 1,000 m buffers and include agricultural land use, cropping intensity, mapped-area coverage, and historical changes. Missing agricultural values remain missing rather than being replaced with zero.


Code

# Load annual crop features, preserving well IDs as text.
crop = pd.read_csv(CROP_PATH, dtype={"gm_well_id": "string"})

# Check the columns required for temporal matching.
required_crop_columns = {"gm_well_id", "crop_year"}

if not required_crop_columns.issubset(crop.columns):
    raise ValueError(
        f"Missing crop columns: {required_crop_columns - set(crop.columns)}"
    )

# Make sure crop years are numeric.
crop["crop_year"] = pd.to_numeric(
    crop["crop_year"], errors="raise"
).astype("Int64")

# Each well must have at most one record per crop year.
if crop.duplicated(["gm_well_id", "crop_year"]).any():
    raise ValueError("Duplicate well-year combinations in crop data.")

# Identify agricultural predictors and coverage metadata.
crop_columns = [
    col for col in crop.columns
    if col not in ["gm_well_id", "crop_year"]
]

print("Crop records:", len(crop))
print("Unique wells:", crop["gm_well_id"].nunique())
print("Available crop years:", sorted(crop["crop_year"].dropna().unique()))
print("Crop feature columns:", len(crop_columns))

6. Assemble and check the table
Static soil and terrain features join by well ID. Climate and crop features join by observation ID. Every join is left-sided and checked to preserve all original samples. Missing values are reported, not filled.


Code
integrated = observations.copy()
integrated, soil_match = checked_left_merge(integrated, soil_features, "gm_well_id", "SSURGO")
integrated, dem_match = checked_left_merge(integrated, dem_features, "gm_well_id", "terrain")


# Match each nitrate observation to the previous year's crop map.
integrated["crop_year"] = (
    integrated["gm_samp_collection_date"].dt.year - 1
).astype("Int64")

# Join crops by well ID and crop year, keeping every nitrate observation.
crop_rows = integrated[
    ["observation_id", "gm_well_id", "crop_year"]
].merge(
    crop,
    on=["gm_well_id", "crop_year"],
    how="left",
    validate="many_to_one",
    sort=False,
    indicator="crop_source_match"
)

# Verify that the crop join preserves all nitrate observations.
if (
    len(crop_rows) != len(integrated)
    or not crop_rows["observation_id"].equals(integrated["observation_id"])
):
    raise AssertionError("Crop join changed nitrate observations.")

# Keep the crop matching status and all crop features.
crop_rows["crop_source_match"] = (
    crop_rows["crop_source_match"].astype("string")
)

actual_crop_matches = int(
    crop_rows["crop_source_match"].eq("both").sum()
)

integrated, crop_join_check = checked_left_merge(
    integrated,
    crop_rows[
        ["observation_id", *crop_columns, "crop_source_match"]
    ],
    "observation_id",
    "historical crop features"
)

# 6b. Final checks and save
# The integrated table is only written if it does not exist yet.
# If it already exists, we compare it with the table we just built
# and report any differences, WITHOUT overwriting the saved file
# (all model results were produced with the saved file).

climate_cols = [
    "historical_mean_annual_precip_mm",
    "previous_3_complete_months_precip_mm",
    "previous_12_complete_months_precip_mm",
    "historical_mean_temperature_c",
    "previous_3_complete_months_temperature_c",
    "previous_12_complete_months_temperature_c",
]

assert integrated["observation_id"].is_unique           # no duplicated samples
assert integrated["crop_source_match"].eq("both").all() # every sample matched a crop record

new_path = (
    paths.MODEL_DATA
)

if new_path.exists():
    # Read the saved table, with the same data types as the new one,
    # so that the comparison is fair
    saved = pd.read_csv(
        new_path,
        dtype={"gm_well_id": "string", "observation_id": "string"},
    )
    for column in integrated.columns:
        if pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(integrated[column]):
            saved[column] = pd.to_datetime(saved[column], errors="raise")
        elif pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(integrated[column]):
            saved[column] = pd.to_numeric(saved[column], errors="raise")

    # For every numeric column, find the largest difference between
    # the saved table and the new one (ignoring tiny rounding noise)
    numeric = [c for c in integrated.columns if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(integrated[c])]
    diffs = (saved[numeric] - integrated[numeric]).abs().max()
    scale = integrated[numeric].abs().max().clip(lower=1)    # compare relative to each column's size
    diffs = diffs[diffs > 1e-9 * scale].sort_values(ascending=False)

    if diffs.empty:
        print("Existing output matches; reusing without writing:", new_path)
    else:
        # Differences found: keep the saved file and show how big they are
        print("Existing output kept unchanged (all model results use it).")
        print("Largest absolute differences vs. the current inputs:")
        print(diffs.head(8).round(4).to_string())
else:
    # First run: no saved table yet, so write it
    integrated.to_csv(new_path, index=False)
    print("Saved:", new_path)

print("Rows, columns:", integrated.shape)
print("Climate columns:", len(climate_cols))

title: Groundwater Feature Integration — Historical Crops (Lag-1)
text:
7. Conclusions

The integrated table has 5,280 nitrate observations from 1,993 wells and 147 columns (2022: 1,455; 2023: 1,298; 2024: 1,252; 2025: 1,275 samples).
Every observation was preserved through all joins, and all 5,280 observations matched a historical crop record (lag-1, 2021–2024 crop maps).
The six PRISM climate features have no missing values.
Missing values are rare except for depth to bedrock (soil_brockdepmin, 73% missing), which is screened out in notebooks/feature_selection.ipynb.
Distance to large rivers was not included because NHD stream-order data were unavailable.

Assumptions and limitations - The one-year crop lag is a consistent modeling assumption, not an established nitrate transport time. - The 2024 DWR crop map is provisional; it feeds the 2025 nitrate samples. - Areas outside DWR-mapped polygons are not treated as zero agriculture; their share is kept as outside_dwr_polygons_pct.

title: Nitrate risk map over entire Salinas Valley
text:
Objective: Predict the probability that groundwater nitrate exceeds 10 mg/L for every grid cell in the Salinas Valley, including areas without sampled wells, using the RandomForestClassifer. Previous modeling approaches (notebooks/classification_models.ipynb) were only concerned with geographic points that had any previous well measurements within 2021-2025.
Steps: 1. Train the final model once: the tuned random forest from classification_models.ipynb (same grid and search), on all training wells (folds 0–3). 2. Build a grid over the Salinas Valley groundwater basin, keeping cells within a set distance of training wells (the model’s domain). 3. Compute the 59 model features for each cell. 4. Predict, group into risk levels. 5. Hybrid version: correct the model with the measurements at nearby wells (residuals within 2 km). 6. Map both versions and save.
Inputs (local only, not in Git): data/soils/soils_huc8_attributes.gpkg, data/elevation/dem_watershed_10m.tif, and the DWR statewide crop map geodatabases (folder set by ERDOS_CROPS_DIR, default Data/Erdos Project/raw/Crops, as in the crop notebook).
Outputs: results/risk_map/risk_map_<cell size>m.csv plus one .png per version (in Git); a GeoPackage with cell polygons and one GeoTIFF per version in data/outputs/ (local, for ArcGIS).
Runtime: the crop overlay is the slow step. Start with TEST_CELLS = 300 to check everything runs, then set it to None for the full map. A 500 m grid has roughly 4 times fewer cells than 250 m.

1. Final model
Cross-validation trained four temporary models (one per fold) only to measure performance; they were not kept. The map needs one model, so the random forest is tuned and trained once on all training wells, with the same grid and search as in classification_models.ipynb (300 trees, settings chosen by Brier score with one spatial fold held out at a time).
The hold-out evaluation in final_results.ipynb is done, so the map model is trained on all wells (FIT_ON = "all"), the usual practice once a model has been evaluated: it adds the hold-out wells, including about half of the East Side Aquifer samples.

title: Nitrate risk map over entire Salinas Valley
text:
2. Grid and model domain
Cell centers inside the Salinas Valley groundwater basin (DWR Bulletin 118 subbasins). Only cells within MAX_DISTANCE_TO_WELL_M of a training well are predicted, so the model is not applied to conditions far from where it learned.


Code
subbasins = gpd.read_file(SUBBASIN_PATH).to_crs(METRIC_CRS)
basin = subbasins.union_all()

wells = train.drop_duplicates("gm_well_id")
wells = gpd.GeoDataFrame(wells[["gm_well_id"]],
                         geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(wells.gm_longitude, wells.gm_latitude),
                         crs=4326).to_crs(METRIC_CRS)
well_xy = np.c_[wells.geometry.x, wells.geometry.y]

xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = basin.bounds
xs = np.arange(xmin + CELL_SIZE_M / 2, xmax, CELL_SIZE_M)
ys = np.arange(ymin + CELL_SIZE_M / 2, ymax, CELL_SIZE_M)
gx, gy = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
centers = gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(gx.ravel(), gy.ravel()), crs=METRIC_CRS)
centers = centers[centers.within(basin)].reset_index(drop=True)

distance, _ = cKDTree(well_xy).query(np.c_[centers.geometry.x, centers.geometry.y])
cells = centers[distance <= MAX_DISTANCE_TO_WELL_M].reset_index(drop=True)

if TEST_CELLS:
    # A compact test area: the cells closest to the median training well
    center = np.median(well_xy, axis=0)
    order = np.argsort(np.hypot(cells.geometry.x - center[0], cells.geometry.y - center[1]))
    cells = cells.iloc[np.sort(order[:TEST_CELLS])].reset_index(drop=True)

cells["gm_well_id"] = [f"C{i:06d}" for i in range(len(cells))]
lonlat = cells.to_crs(4326).geometry
cells["gm_latitude"], cells["gm_longitude"] = lonlat.y.to_numpy(), lonlat.x.to_numpy()
cells["x"], cells["y"] = cells.geometry.x, cells.geometry.y

print(f"{len(centers):,} cells in the basin | {int((distance <= MAX_DISTANCE_TO_WELL_M).sum()):,} within "
      f"{MAX_DISTANCE_TO_WELL_M / 1000:g} km of a training well | {len(cells):,} cells to predict"
      + (" (test run)" if TEST_CELLS else ""))

3. Features for each cell
Each block reproduces the method used for the wells.

3.1 Soils (SSURGO, area-weighted within 500 m)


Code
def soil_features(points, soils, radius=500, batch_size=500):
    """Area-weighted SSURGO attributes within a circle around each point (as in all_merge_final)."""
    numeric_fields = ["slopegradwta", "brockdepmin", "aws0150wta"]
    category_fields = ["drclassdcd", "hydgrpdcd"]
    category_values = {name: sorted(soils[name].dropna().unique(), key=str) for name in category_fields}
    columns = numeric_fields + category_fields
    out = []
    for start in range(0, len(points), batch_size):
        batch = points.iloc[start:start + batch_size][["gm_well_id", "geometry"]].copy()
        batch.geometry = batch.buffer(radius)
        candidates = gpd.sjoin(batch, soils[columns + ["geometry"]], how="inner", predicate="intersects")
        if candidates.empty:
            pairs = candidates.assign(_area=pd.Series(dtype="float64"))
        else:
            pieces = shapely.intersection(candidates.geometry.array,
                                          soils.geometry.array.take(candidates["index_right"].to_numpy(dtype=int)))
            area = shapely.area(pieces)
            keep = np.isfinite(area) & (area > 0)
            pairs = candidates.loc[keep].assign(_area=area[keep])

        table = pd.DataFrame({"gm_well_id": batch["gm_well_id"].to_numpy()})
        buffer_area = batch.geometry.area.to_numpy()
        mapped = table.gm_well_id.map(pairs.groupby("gm_well_id")["_area"].sum()).fillna(0.0)
        table["soil_mapped_coverage_pct"] = 100 * mapped.to_numpy() / buffer_area
        for name in numeric_fields:
            valid = pairs[pairs[name].notna()]
            valid_area = valid.groupby("gm_well_id")["_area"].sum()
            weighted = (valid[name] * valid["_area"]).groupby(valid["gm_well_id"]).sum()
            table[f"soil_{name}"] = table.gm_well_id.map(weighted / valid_area).to_numpy()
        for name in category_fields:
            valid = pairs.dropna(subset=[name])
            valid_area = table.gm_well_id.map(valid.groupby("gm_well_id")["_area"].sum())
            by_category = valid.groupby(["gm_well_id", name], observed=True)["_area"].sum()
            for category in category_values[name]:
                label = str(category).strip().lower().replace(" ", "_").replace("/", "_")
                try:
                    area_c = by_category.xs(category, level=name)
                except KeyError:
                    area_c = pd.Series(dtype="float64")
                pct = 100 * table.gm_well_id.map(area_c).fillna(0.0) / valid_area
                table[f"soil_{name}_pct_{label}"] = pct.where(valid_area > 0).to_numpy()
        out.append(table)
    return pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True)


t0 = time.time()
soils = gpd.read_file(SOIL_PATH).to_crs(METRIC_CRS).reset_index(drop=True)
for name in ["slopegradwta", "brockdepmin", "aws0150wta"]:
    soils[name] = pd.to_numeric(soils[name], errors="coerce")
cell_soils = soil_features(cells, soils)
print(f"Soils done in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s | mean mapped coverage {cell_soils.soil_mapped_coverage_pct.mean():.1f}%")

terrain = []

def climate_for_date(point_data, sample_date):
    """Climate features from complete months/years before sample_date (as in all_merge_final)."""
    result = {}
    sample_month = sample_date.to_period("M")
    prior = point_data.loc[point_data.date.dt.to_period("M") < sample_month].copy()
    prior["period"] = prior.date.dt.to_period("M")
    for window in [3, 12]:
        periods = pd.period_range(end=sample_month - 1, periods=window, freq="M")
        values = prior.set_index("period").reindex(periods)
        complete = values.date.notna().all()
        result[f"previous_{window}_complete_months_precip_mm"] = values.precip_mm.sum() if complete else np.nan
        result[f"previous_{window}_complete_months_temperature_c"] = values.tmean_c.mean() if complete else np.nan
    prior["year"] = prior.date.dt.year
    full_years = prior.groupby("year").date.nunique()
    history = prior[prior.year.isin(full_years[full_years == 12].index)]
    result["historical_mean_annual_precip_mm"] = history.groupby("year").precip_mm.sum().mean()
    result["historical_mean_temperature_c"] = history.tmean_c.mean()
    return result

3.4 Land use (DWR crop maps, 500 m and 1,000 m)
Crop shares, crop cycles, multicropping and the unmapped share for CROP_YEAR, plus the annual change from CROP_YEAR - 1. The functions are copied from crop_mapping_annual_2021_2024.ipynb; cells are processed in batches.


Code
RADII = (500, 1000)
GROUPS = ["veg_berry", "vineyard", "orchard", "grain_field_pasture", "idle_fallow", "urban"]
FARMED = ["veg_berry", "vineyard", "orchard", "grain_field_pasture"]
CLASS_GROUP = {
    "T": "veg_berry", "V": "vineyard", "D": "orchard", "C": "orchard",
    "Y": "orchard", "YP": "orchard", "G": "grain_field_pasture",
    "F": "grain_field_pasture", "P": "grain_field_pasture",
    "R": "grain_field_pasture", "I": "idle_fallow", "X": "idle_fallow",
}
CYCLES = {"S": 1, "D": 2, "T": 3, "Q": 4}


def require(ok, message):
    if not ok:
        raise ValueError(message)


def find_gdb(root, token):
    matches = [p.parent for p in Path(root).rglob("a00000001.gdbtable")
               if token.lower() in p.parent.name.lower()]
    require(len(matches) == 1, f"Expected one GDB for {token}; found {matches}")
    return matches[0]


def read_crop_map(path, boundary):
    layer = pyogrio.list_layers(path)[0, 0]
    info = pyogrio.read_info(path, layer=layer)
    xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = boundary.total_bounds
    to_source = Transformer.from_crs(METRIC_CRS, info["crs"], always_xy=True)
    bbox = to_source.transform_bounds(xmin - 1001, ymin - 1001, xmax + 1001, ymax + 1001, densify_pts=41)
    data = pyogrio.read_dataframe(path, layer=layer, bbox=bbox)
    data.geometry = data.geometry.force_2d().to_crs(METRIC_CRS).buffer(0)
    letters = data.SYMB_CLASS.astype("string").str.split("|").str[0].str.strip().str.upper()
    data["crop_group"] = letters.map(CLASS_GROUP)
    data.loc[letters.str.startswith("U", na=False), "crop_group"] = "urban"
    data["crop_cycles"] = data.MULTIUSE.astype("string").str.strip().map(CYCLES)
    return data.reset_index(drop=True)


def summarize(points, candidates, radius):
    """Crop features within a circle around each point (from the crop mapping notebook)."""
    circles = points[["gm_well_id", "geometry"]].copy()
    circles.geometry = circles.buffer(radius, quad_segs=16)
    grouped = candidates.dissolve(by=["crop_group", "crop_cycles"]).reset_index()
    pieces = gpd.overlay(circles, grouped[["crop_group", "crop_cycles", "geometry"]],
                         how="intersection", keep_geom_type=True)
    pieces["area_m2"] = pieces.area
    ids = pd.Index(points.gm_well_id.astype("string"), name="gm_well_id")
    areas = pieces.pivot_table(index="gm_well_id", columns="crop_group", values="area_m2", aggfunc="sum")
    areas = areas.reindex(index=ids, columns=GROUPS, fill_value=0).fillna(0)
    mapped = pieces.groupby("gm_well_id").geometry.apply(lambda s: s.union_all().area).reindex(ids, fill_value=0)
    circle_area = np.pi * radius**2
    buffer_area = pd.Series(circles.area.to_numpy(), index=ids)

    table = pd.DataFrame(index=ids)
    for group in GROUPS:
        table[f"pct_{group}_{radius}m"] = areas[group] / circle_area * 100
    table[f"pct_cropland_{radius}m"] = areas[FARMED].sum(axis=1) / circle_area * 100
    farm = pieces[pieces.crop_group.isin(FARMED)]
    farm_area = farm.groupby("gm_well_id").area_m2.sum().reindex(ids, fill_value=0)
    weighted = (farm.area_m2 * farm.crop_cycles).groupby(farm.gm_well_id).sum()
    table[f"crop_cycles_{radius}m"] = weighted.reindex(ids) / farm_area.replace(0, np.nan)
    multi = farm[farm.crop_cycles.ge(2)].groupby("gm_well_id").area_m2.sum()
    table[f"pct_multicrop_{radius}m"] = multi.reindex(ids, fill_value=0) / circle_area * 100
    table[f"dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_{radius}m"] = mapped / buffer_area * 100
    table[f"outside_dwr_polygons_pct_{radius}m"] = (buffer_area - mapped).clip(lower=0) / buffer_area * 100
    no_map = mapped.le(1e-8)
    crop_columns = [c for c in table if c.startswith("pct_") or c.startswith("crop_cycles_")]
    table.loc[no_map, crop_columns] = np.nan
    return table


def crop_features_for_year(year, points, batch_size=500):
    crop_map = read_crop_map(find_gdb(CROPS_DIR, str(year)), points)
    tables = []
    for radius in RADII:
        parts = []
        for start in range(0, len(points), batch_size):
            batch = points.iloc[start:start + batch_size]
            support = batch.buffer(radius).union_all()
            candidates = crop_map[crop_map.intersects(support)]
            if candidates.empty:
                parts.append(pd.DataFrame(index=pd.Index(batch.gm_well_id.astype("string"), name="gm_well_id")))
            else:
                parts.append(summarize(batch, candidates, radius))
        table = pd.concat(parts)
        # Cells with no DWR polygon at all: nothing mapped (not zero agriculture)
        table[f"dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_{radius}m"] = table[f"dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_{radius}m"].fillna(0.0)
        table[f"outside_dwr_polygons_pct_{radius}m"] = table[f"outside_dwr_polygons_pct_{radius}m"].fillna(100.0)
        tables.append(table)
    return pd.concat(tables, axis=1)


t0 = time.time()
current = crop_features_for_year(CROP_YEAR, cells)
previous = crop_features_for_year(CROP_YEAR - 1, cells).reindex(current.index)

cell_crops = current.copy()
for radius in RADII:
    both = (current[f"dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_{radius}m"].gt(0)
            & previous[f"dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_{radius}m"].gt(0))
    for group in [*GROUPS, "cropland", "multicrop"]:
        col = f"pct_{group}_{radius}m"
        cell_crops[f"delta_{group}_pp_{radius}m"] = (current[col] - previous[col]).where(both)
    col = f"dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_{radius}m"
    cell_crops[f"delta_dwr_polygon_footprint_pp_{radius}m"] = (current[col] - previous[col]).where(both)
cell_crops = cell_crops.reset_index()
print(f"Crops done in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

text:
4. Assemble features and predict

text:
5. Hybrid version: model + nearby measurements
The model does not use the measurement at a location to predict that location. Near sampled wells, however, the measurements carry information the model misses: the model’s errors (residuals) at wells closer than ~1 km are correlated (about 0.58 under 250 m, 0.23 at 0.5–1 km, near 0 beyond 2 km).
The hybrid corrects each cell with the residuals of training wells within 2 km, weighting closer wells more (a simple form of residual kriging): 1. Out-of-fold predictions at the training wells from the same random forest, saved by classification_models.ipynb (each well is predicted by a model that did not see it). 2. Residual per well = measured exceedance (0/1) minus predicted probability, averaged over the well’s samples. 3. Correction per cell = weighted average of nearby residuals, with weights that decay with distance.
In a leave-one-well-out check with an earlier version of the random forest, this raised the AUC from 0.82 to 0.89. The gain only applies near sampled wells; far from them, the hybrid equals the model.
How several wells are combined. For each cell, every training well within 2 km of the cell center contributes its residual (each well’s residual is first averaged over its samples). The correction is sum(weight × residual) / (1 + sum(weights)): wells at the same distance count equally, wells that disagree partly cancel out, and the 1 + keeps the correction small when there are only a few, distant wells. There are no buffers around wells; the search is around each cell center.


Code
# Out-of-fold predictions of the same random forest at the training wells, saved by classification_models.ipynb
# (each well predicted by a model that did not see it)
oof = pd.read_csv(predictions_path("classification", SPLIT, True), dtype={"gm_well_id": "string"})
oof = oof.rename(columns={"Random forest": "oof_probability"})

# Residual = measured exceedance (0/1) minus predicted probability, averaged per well
residuals = (oof.assign(residual=oof["exceeds"] - oof["oof_probability"])
             .groupby("gm_well_id").agg(lat=("gm_latitude", "first"), lon=("gm_longitude", "first"),
                                        residual=("residual", "mean")))
residuals = gpd.GeoDataFrame(residuals, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(residuals.lon, residuals.lat),
                             crs=4326).to_crs(METRIC_CRS)
print(f"Residuals at {len(residuals):,} wells | mean {residuals.residual.mean():+.3f} "
      "(near 0 = no average bias)")


Residuals at 1,622 wells | mean -0.014 (near 0 = no average bias)


How the distance weights were chosen. The weights come from how similar the model’s errors are between pairs of wells at different distances (a correlogram): nearby wells tend to share errors, distant wells do not. The curve below is the weight used for one well, 0.6 × exp(−distance / 700 m), drawn over the observed correlations.


Code
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree as _Tree

res_xy = np.c_[residuals.geometry.x, residuals.geometry.y]
res_values = residuals.residual.to_numpy()
pairs = _Tree(res_xy).query_pairs(4000, output_type="ndarray")
pair_distance = np.hypot(*(res_xy[pairs[:, 0]] - res_xy[pairs[:, 1]]).T)
edges = [0, 250, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 3000, 4000]
correlogram = []
for low, high in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
    in_bin = (pair_distance >= low) & (pair_distance < high)
    correlogram.append({"distance_m": (low + high) / 2, "pairs": int(in_bin.sum()),
                        "correlation": np.corrcoef(res_values[pairs[in_bin, 0]], res_values[pairs[in_bin, 1]])[0, 1]})
correlogram = pd.DataFrame(correlogram)
display(correlogram.round(2))

d = np.linspace(0, 4000, 200)
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
plt.plot(correlogram.distance_m, correlogram.correlation, "o-", label="Observed correlation of well residuals")
plt.plot(d, 0.6 * np.exp(-d / 700), "--", label="Weight used: 0.6 × exp(−d / 700 m)")
plt.axvline(2000, color="gray", linestyle=":", label="Search radius (2 km)")
plt.xlabel("Distance between wells (m)")

RESIDUAL_RANGE_M = 700     # residual correlation decays with distance (about 0 beyond ~2 km)
RESIDUAL_MAX_CORR = 0.6    # correlation between residuals of very close wells
SEARCH_RADIUS_M = 2000

well_xy = np.c_[residuals.geometry.x, residuals.geometry.y]
tree = cKDTree(well_xy)
cell_xy = np.c_[cells.x, cells.y]
correction = np.zeros(len(cells))
for i, neighbors in enumerate(tree.query_ball_point(cell_xy, SEARCH_RADIUS_M)):
    if neighbors:
        distance = np.hypot(*(well_xy[neighbors] - cell_xy[i]).T)
        weight = RESIDUAL_MAX_CORR * np.exp(-distance / RESIDUAL_RANGE_M)
        correction[i] = (weight * residuals.residual.to_numpy()[neighbors]).sum() / (1 + weight.sum())

cells["hybrid_correction"] = correction
cells["hybrid_probability"] = (cells["model_probability"] + correction).clip(0, 1)
cells["hybrid_risk_level"] = pd.cut(cells.hybrid_probability, RISK_BINS, right=False, labels=RISK_LABELS)

print(f"Mean absolute correction: {np.abs(correction).mean():.3f}")
display(pd.crosstab(cells.model_risk_level, cells.hybrid_risk_level, margins=True,
                    rownames=["Model"], colnames=["Hybrid"]))

text:
8. Notes and limitations

Probabilities: the random forest is tuned for the Brier score (no class weights), so its probabilities can be read as probabilities. Low/Moderate/High is a display choice; the team’s decision threshold for calling an exceedance can be shown as a two-color map.
Each cell is a hypothetical domestic well sampled on REFERENCE_DATE, with the CROP_YEAR crop map. Well depth is unknown, as in the training data.
Model domain: cells farther than MAX_DISTANCE_TO_WELL_M from any training well, or with no DWR crop polygons within 1 km, are not predicted.
Location effects: subbasin indicators carry much of the predictive power, so the map mostly reflects differences between aquifers, refined by local land use and soils.
The hybrid only changes cells near sampled wells (within 2 km); elsewhere it equals the model. Its residual weights (700 m range, 0.6 maximum correlation) were set by eye from the residual correlogram, not optimized. With FIT_ON = "all", the residuals come from the cross-validation predictions of folds 0–3 (hold-out wells contribute no residuals), while the map model also learned from the hold-out wells.
Not validated as a map: performance was measured at wells (10 km spatial folds). The fold 4 holdout is reserved for the final evaluation of the chosen model.
Monitoring priority marks predicted exceedances with no sampled well within 1 km; it ignores where domestic wells actually are, which would be the next layer to add.

title: Post-Hoc Robustness Check: Subbasin-Balanced Hold-Outs
text:
Objective: Check how much the hold-out score depends on which area ends up in the hold-out. The official hold-out (fold 4 of the 10km_subbasin split) concentrates about half of the East Side Aquifer samples, our most contaminated subbasin, and scored lower than cross-validation (AUC 0.741 vs. 0.827).
This is a post-hoc analysis, not a replacement for the official result. It was designed after seeing the official hold-out score, and every well here, including the official hold-out wells, has already been used during the project. The official hold-out remains the result we report; this notebook only describes how much the score varies when the test area is drawn so that every subbasin is represented in proportion.
Design (no new modeling decisions): 1. Same data, features (load_model_data(subbasin=True)), 10 km grid cells, model (tuned random forest from the consolidated notebooks) and threshold (0.4) as final_results.ipynb. 2. Each repeat draws a new hold-out: within each subbasin, whole 10 km cells are picked at random until about 20% of that subbasin’s samples are held out. 3. The remaining data are split into 4 spatial folds (whole cells, balanced on exceedance) for the hyperparameter search; the model is fit on them and scored once on that repeat’s hold-out. 4. Several repeats with different random seeds show the range of hold-out scores.
Runtime: each repeat tunes two random forests; about 3–5 minutes per repeat.

title: Post-Hoc Robustness Check: Subbasin-Balanced Hold-Outs
text:
2. Draw subbasin-balanced hold-outs
Within each subbasin, cells are shuffled and added to the hold-out while that subbasin’s held-out samples stay below the target share; a cell is always kept whole. Small subbasins with only a few cells may end up with slightly more or less than the target.


Code
def balanced_holdout(seed):
    """Cells chosen so that each subbasin contributes about HOLDOUT_SHARE of its samples."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    chosen = []
    for name, cells_in in cell_subbasin.groupby(cell_subbasin):
        order = rng.permutation(cells_in.index.to_numpy())
        target = HOLDOUT_SHARE * cell_samples[order].sum()
        held = 0
        for cell in order:
            if held + cell_samples[cell] / 2 <= target:    # add the cell if at least half of it fits
                chosen.append(cell)
                held += cell_samples[cell]
    return data["cell"].isin(chosen).to_numpy()


holdouts = {seed: balanced_holdout(seed) for seed in range(N_REPEATS)}
balance = pd.DataFrame({f"repeat {s}": data[h].groupby("subbasin_name").size() / data.groupby("subbasin_name").size()
                        for s, h in holdouts.items()}).fillna(0)
balance.loc["All samples"] = [h.mean() for h in holdouts.values()]
balance.loc["Share above 10 mg/L (hold-out)"] = [data.loc[h, "exceeds"].mean() for h in holdouts.values()]
official = data["holdout"].to_numpy()
balance["official hold-out"] = list((data[official].groupby("subbasin_name").size()
                                     / data.groupby("subbasin_name").size()).reindex(balance.index[:-2]).fillna(0)) \
                               + [official.mean(), data.loc[official, "exceeds"].mean()]
print("Share of each subbasin's samples in the hold-out:")
display(balance.round(2))

3. Fit and score each repeat
For each repeat: 4 spatial folds on the remaining data for the hyperparameter search (same search as the model notebooks), one fit, one score on that repeat’s hold-out.


Code
def fit_search(make_search, dev, target, folds):
    search = make_search()
    search.fit(dev[FEATURES], dev[target], groups=folds)
    return search.best_estimator_


rows = []
for seed, is_holdout in holdouts.items():
    dev, test = data[~is_holdout].reset_index(drop=True), data[is_holdout].reset_index(drop=True)
    folds = splits.spatial_folds(dev["cell"], dev["exceeds"], n_splits=4, seed=seed)

    clf = fit_search(lambda: tuned(RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=300, random_state=0, n_jobs=1),
                                   RF_GRID, "neg_brier_score", n_iter=10), dev, "exceeds", folds)
    prob = clf.predict_proba(test[FEATURES])[:, 1]
    called = (prob >= THRESHOLD).astype(int)
    base_rate = dev["exceeds"].mean()

    reg = fit_search(lambda: tuned(RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=300, random_state=0, n_jobs=1),
                                   RF_GRID, "neg_root_mean_squared_error", n_iter=10), dev, "log_nitrate", folds)
    pred = reg.predict(test[FEATURES])
    dummy = DummyRegressor().fit(dev[FEATURES], dev["log_nitrate"]).predict(test[FEATURES])

    rows.append({
        "repeat": seed, "holdout_samples": len(test), "holdout_share_above_10": test["exceeds"].mean(),
        "auc": roc_auc_score(test["exceeds"], prob),
        "brier_skill": 1 - brier_score_loss(test["exceeds"], prob)
                       / brier_score_loss(test["exceeds"], np.full(len(test), base_rate)),
        "recall": recall_score(test["exceeds"], called), "precision": precision_score(test["exceeds"], called),
        "f1": f1_score(test["exceeds"], called),
        "rmse_log": root_mean_squared_error(test["log_nitrate"], pred),
        "dummy_rmse_log": root_mean_squared_error(test["log_nitrate"], dummy),
        "r2": r2_score(test["log_nitrate"], pred),
    })
    print(f"Repeat {seed}: AUC {rows[-1]['auc']:.3f} | R² {rows[-1]['r2']:.3f} | "
          f"{len(test):,} hold-out samples, {rows[-1]['holdout_share_above_10']:.0%} above 10 mg/L")

robustness = pd.DataFrame(rows)
robustness.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "subbasin_balanced_holdouts.csv", index=False)

title: Post-Hoc Robustness Check: Subbasin-Balanced Hold-Outs
text:
5. Conclusions

Balanced hold-outs reproduce cross-validation performance. Across 5 subbasin-balanced hold-outs, the random forest’s AUC ranged from 0.800 to 0.867 (mean 0.838), close to the cross-validation mean (0.827). Brier skill (mean 0.290 vs. 0.291) and R² for log nitrate (mean 0.365 vs. 0.343) also match cross-validation.
The official hold-out is below every balanced repeat (AUC 0.741 vs. a minimum of 0.800; R² 0.170 vs. a minimum of 0.290). This is consistent with its test area being harder: it contains about half of the East Side Aquifer samples, our most contaminated subbasin, and 42% of its samples exceed 10 mg/L versus about 30% elsewhere.
At the 0.4 threshold, the balanced hold-outs detect 69–89% of exceeding samples (mean 80%) with 54–64% precision, similar to the official hold-out’s 74% recall and 59% precision.
Interpretation: the model generalizes to unseen areas about as well as cross-validation suggests when every subbasin is represented, but it performs worse where a heavily contaminated subbasin is under-represented in training.
Caveat: this check was designed after seeing the official result and reuses wells already used in the project, so it describes variability; it is not an independent test. The official hold-out score is the one we report, alongside cross-validation. A clean test of a subbasin-balanced design would need new data (e.g., 2026 samples).

title: Groundwater spatial sampling and validation diagnostics
text:
This notebook uses the existing cleaned nitrate data to explore monitoring locations, nitrate differences between nearby wells, temporal coverage, and possible train/test leakage. It is exploratory: it does not train a model, select a validation design, change values, merge wells, remove rows, or regenerate buffers.
Distinct well IDs stay separate, including IDs at the same coordinates. The source observations and years remain intact.

title: Groundwater spatial sampling and validation diagnostics
section: 3. Compare nitrate at nearby wells in similar periods
text:
3. Compare nitrate at nearby wells in similar periods
For same-day comparisons, repeated results for one well and date are averaged only in a temporary table. For same-year comparisons, each well’s annual mean is used. Original rows stay unchanged. The comparisons include different IDs up to 1,000 m apart and are grouped by distance band. Pair-periods reuse wells, so they are not independent observations; proximity does not establish duplicate wells.


Code
DISTANCE_EDGES = [0, 20, 30, 100, 500, 1_000.000001]
DISTANCE_LABELS = ["0?20 m", "20?30 m", "30?100 m", "100?500 m", "500?1,000 m"]

def nearby_period_pairs(period_data, period_name):
    """Summarize within-well period values, then compare distinct nearby IDs."""
    pair_rows = []
    for period, group in period_data.groupby("period", sort=False):
        summaries = group.groupby("gm_well_id", as_index=False).agg(
            nitrate_mg_L=("nitrate_mg_L", "mean"),
            source_records=("nitrate_mg_L", "size"),
            gm_longitude=("gm_longitude", "first"),
            gm_latitude=("gm_latitude", "first"),
        )
        if len(summaries) < 2:
            continue
        points = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
            summaries,
            geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(summaries.gm_longitude, summaries.gm_latitude),
            crs="EPSG:4326",
        ).to_crs(METRIC_CRS)
        xy = np.column_stack([points.geometry.x, points.geometry.y])
        pairs = cKDTree(xy).query_pairs(r=1_000, output_type="ndarray")
        if len(pairs) == 0:
            continue
        for left, right in pairs:
            a, b = summaries.iloc[left], summaries.iloc[right]
            pair_rows.append({
                "period": period,
                "well_id_a": a.gm_well_id,
                "well_id_b": b.gm_well_id,
                "distance_m": float(np.linalg.norm(xy[left] - xy[right])),
                "nitrate_a": float(a.nitrate_mg_L),
                "nitrate_b": float(b.nitrate_mg_L),
                "absolute_difference_mg_L": float(abs(a.nitrate_mg_L - b.nitrate_mg_L)),
                "records_a_summarized": int(a.source_records),
                "records_b_summarized": int(b.source_records),
            })
    pairs = pd.DataFrame(pair_rows)
    if pairs.empty:
        return pairs
    pairs["distance_band"] = pd.cut(
        pairs["distance_m"], bins=DISTANCE_EDGES, labels=DISTANCE_LABELS,
        right=False, include_lowest=True,
    )
    pairs["well_pair"] = pairs.apply(lambda row: "|".join(sorted([row.well_id_a, row.well_id_b])), axis=1)
    pairs["comparison_type"] = period_name
    return pairs

same_day_pairs = nearby_period_pairs(same_day_data, "Same sampling date")

def summarize_pairs(pairs):

text:
4. Compare changes within and between nearby wells
The notebook summarizes annual means by well ID, calculates each well’s range across those means, and compares it with same-year differences between nearby IDs. It also counts sampling dates and years per well. Ranges depend on when and how often a well was sampled, and these summaries use different samples; they are descriptive context, not a formal variance decomposition.


Code

).agg(

)

    years_observed=("year", "nunique"),
    first_year=("year", "min"),
    last_year=("year", "max"),

).reset_index()

title: Groundwater spatial sampling and validation diagnostics
text:
5. Illustrative train/test proximity checks
With a fixed seed, the notebook compares a random observation split, a split grouped by well ID, and a split holding out complete 5 km grid cells. It reports well overlap, row and well counts, nearest training-well distances, proximity thresholds, and year coverage. No model is fitted and no split is recommended. Random row splits can put the same repeatedly sampled well in both sets; grouping prevents that, while nearby different wells can still cross the split. Block edges can also remain close.


Code
RANDOM_SEED = 42
TEST_FRACTION = 0.20
PROXIMITY_THRESHOLDS_M = [20, 30, 100, 500, 1_000]
row_index = np.arange(len(observations))
random_train_rows, random_test_rows = train_test_split(
    row_index, test_size=TEST_FRACTION, random_state=RANDOM_SEED, shuffle=True
)
group_splitter = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=TEST_FRACTION, random_state=RANDOM_SEED)
group_train_rows, group_test_rows = next(group_splitter.split(
    row_index, groups=observations["gm_well_id"]
))

site_frame = well_sites[["gm_well_id", "geometry"]].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

def block_partition(site_data, block_size_m, offset_fraction=0.0, seed=RANDOM_SEED):
    xy = np.column_stack([site_data.geometry.x, site_data.geometry.y])
    offset = block_size_m * offset_fraction
    block_x = np.floor((xy[:, 0] - offset) / block_size_m).astype(int)
    block_y = np.floor((xy[:, 1] - offset) / block_size_m).astype(int)
    block_id = pd.Series([f"{x}:{y}" for x, y in zip(block_x, block_y)], index=site_data.index)
    split = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=TEST_FRACTION, random_state=seed)
    train_i, test_i = next(split.split(site_data, groups=block_id))
    return site_data.iloc[train_i].gm_well_id.tolist(), site_data.iloc[test_i].gm_well_id.tolist(), block_id

def diagnose_split(name, train_rows, test_rows, train_site_ids=None, test_site_ids=None, block_ids=None):
    train_rows = np.asarray(train_rows, dtype=int)
    test_rows = np.asarray(test_rows, dtype=int)
    if train_site_ids is None:
        train_site_ids = observations.iloc[train_rows].gm_well_id.unique().tolist()
        test_site_ids = observations.iloc[test_rows].gm_well_id.unique().tolist()
    train_set, test_set = set(train_site_ids), set(test_site_ids)
    train_points = site_frame[site_frame.gm_well_id.isin(train_set)].reset_index(drop=True)
    test_points = site_frame[site_frame.gm_well_id.isin(test_set)].reset_index(drop=True)
    xy_train = np.column_stack([train_points.geometry.x, train_points.geometry.y])
    xy_test = np.column_stack([test_points.geometry.x, test_points.geometry.y])
    tree = cKDTree(xy_train)
    k = min(2, len(train_points))
    dist, idx = tree.query(xy_test, k=k)
    if k == 1:
        dist = np.asarray(dist).reshape(-1, 1)
        idx = np.asarray(idx).reshape(-1, 1)
    nearest_different = []
    for row, test_id in enumerate(test_points.gm_well_id):
        candidates = [(float(dist[row, j]), train_points.gm_well_id.iloc[int(idx[row, j])]) for j in range(k)]
        different = [value for value, train_id in candidates if train_id != test_id]
        nearest_different.append(min(different) if different else np.nan)
    nearest_different = np.asarray(nearest_different, dtype=float)
    train_obs = observations.iloc[train_rows]
    test_obs = observations.iloc[test_rows]
    years_train = sorted(train_obs.gm_samp_collection_date.dt.year.unique())
    years_test = sorted(test_obs.gm_samp_collection_date.dt.year.unique())
    result = {
        "strategy": name,
        "train_observations": len(train_rows), "test_observations": len(test_rows),
        "train_wells": len(train_set), "test_wells": len(test_set),
        "well_ID_overlap": len(train_set & test_set),
        "min_distance_different_wells_m": float(np.nanmin(nearest_different)),
        "median_nearest_training_well_m": float(np.nanmedian(nearest_different)),
        "train_years": f"{years_train[0]}?{years_train[-1]} ({len(years_train)})",
        "test_years": f"{years_test[0]}?{years_test[-1]} ({len(years_test)})",
    }
    for threshold in PROXIMITY_THRESHOLDS_M:
        result[f"test_wells_with_train_within_{threshold}m_pct"] = 100 * np.mean(nearest_different <= threshold)
    if block_ids is not None:
        result["train_blocks"] = block_ids.loc[site_frame.gm_well_id.isin(train_set)].nunique()
        result["test_blocks"] = block_ids.loc[site_frame.gm_well_id.isin(test_set)].nunique()
    return result

random_metrics = diagnose_split("Random observations", random_train_rows, random_test_rows)
group_metrics = diagnose_split("Group by well ID", group_train_rows, group_test_rows)
block_train_ids, block_test_ids, block_ids_5km = block_partition(site_frame, 5_000)
block_train_rows = np.flatnonzero(observations.gm_well_id.isin(block_train_ids).to_numpy())
block_test_rows = np.flatnonzero(observations.gm_well_id.isin(block_test_ids).to_numpy())
block_metrics = diagnose_split("5 km spatial blocks (origin grid)", block_train_rows, block_test_rows, block_train_ids, block_test_ids, block_ids_5km)
split_diagnostics = pd.DataFrame([random_metrics, group_metrics, block_metrics])
display(split_diagnostics.round(2))


fig = go.Figure()
for threshold in PROXIMITY_THRESHOLDS_M:
    col = f"test_wells_with_train_within_{threshold}m_pct"
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=split_diagnostics["strategy"], y=split_diagnostics[col], name=f"? {threshold} m"))
fig.update_layout(barmode="group", height=450, title="Test-well proximity to a different training well", yaxis_title="Test wells (%)", xaxis_title="Illustrative split")
display(fig)

section: 6. Compare block sizes and grid origins
text:
6. Compare block sizes and grid origins
The notebook compares 1, 5, and 10 km square grids from the origin and a half-cell offset. For each candidate, a fixed-seed 20% block holdout is drawn. The table reports occupied blocks, wells and observations in each set, balance, and cross-set proximity. These are candidates for discussion, not tuned choices or a final validation design.


Code
block_results = []
block_assignments = {}
for size_m in [1_000, 5_000, 10_000]:
    for offset_fraction, label in [(0.0, "origin"), (0.5, "half-cell offset")]:
        train_ids, test_ids, ids_by_site = block_partition(
            site_frame, size_m, offset_fraction=offset_fraction, seed=RANDOM_SEED
        )
        train_rows = np.flatnonzero(observations.gm_well_id.isin(train_ids).to_numpy())
        test_rows = np.flatnonzero(observations.gm_well_id.isin(test_ids).to_numpy())
        metrics = diagnose_split(
            f"{size_m/1000:g} km, {label}", train_rows, test_rows,
            train_ids, test_ids, ids_by_site,
        )
        metrics["block_size_km"] = size_m / 1_000
        metrics["grid_origin"] = label
        metrics["occupied_blocks"] = ids_by_site.nunique()
        metrics["test_observation_share_pct"] = 100 * len(test_rows) / len(observations)
        block_results.append(metrics)
        block_assignments[(size_m, label)] = (train_ids, test_ids)
block_comparison = pd.DataFrame(block_results)
display(block_comparison[[
    "block_size_km", "grid_origin", "occupied_blocks", "train_blocks", "test_blocks",
    "train_wells", "test_wells", "train_observations", "test_observations",
    "test_observation_share_pct", "well_ID_overlap", "min_distance_different_wells_m",
    "median_nearest_training_well_m", *[f"test_wells_with_train_within_{x}m_pct" for x in [20,30,100,500,1000]],
]].round(2))

title: Groundwater spatial sampling and validation diagnostics
text:
7. Keep three tasks separate
Spatial declustering changes how locations represent a target population or surface. Spatial cross-validation changes how observations are assigned to training and test sets. Record deduplication removes records only when identifiers and provenance establish that they are duplicates. Nearby wells can be distinct and have different nitrate values, so distance alone does not justify weighting or deletion.
The analyses retain every nitrate row and year. They describe location density, observed proximity, concentration differences, and illustrative split behavior. They do not establish duplicates, causal spatial effects, an optimal block size, declustering weights, or expected model performance. Discuss the prediction target and deployment area before choosing an approach.

def require(ok, message):
    if not ok:
        raise ValueError(message)


def sha256(path):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with Path(path).open("rb") as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def find_gdb(root, token):
    matches = [p.parent for p in root.rglob("a00000001.gdbtable")
               if token.lower() in p.parent.name.lower()]
    require(len(matches) == 1, f"Expected one GDB for {token}; found {matches}")
    return matches[0]


def read_crop_map(path, boundary):
    layer = pyogrio.list_layers(path)[0, 0]
    info = pyogrio.read_info(path, layer=layer)
    require(info["crs"] is not None, f"Missing CRS: {path}")
    required = {"UniqueID", "SYMB_CLASS", "MULTIUSE", "COUNTY"}
    require(required <= set(info["fields"]), f"Unexpected source schema: {path}")
    xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = boundary.total_bounds
    to_source = Transformer.from_crs(METRIC_CRS, info["crs"], always_xy=True)
    bbox = to_source.transform_bounds(xmin - 1001, ymin - 1001,
                                      xmax + 1001, ymax + 1001,
                                      densify_pts=41)
    data = pyogrio.read_dataframe(path, layer=layer, bbox=bbox, fid_as_index=True)
    require(data.index.is_unique and data.UniqueID.notna().all()
            and data.UniqueID.is_unique, f"Duplicate/missing source IDs: {path}")
    require(data.geometry.notna().all() and (~data.geometry.is_empty).all(),
            f"Missing source geometry: {path}")
    data.geometry = data.geometry.force_2d().to_crs(METRIC_CRS).buffer(0)
    require(data.is_valid.all(), f"Invalid geometry after repair: {path}")
    letters = (data.SYMB_CLASS.astype("string").str.split("|").str[0]
               .str.strip().str.upper())
    unknown = sorted(set(letters.dropna()) - set(CLASS_GROUP) - {"U", "UL"})
    require(not unknown and letters.notna().all(),
            f"Unreviewed DWR crop classes in {path}: {unknown}")
    data["crop_group"] = letters.map(CLASS_GROUP)
    data.loc[letters.str.startswith("U", na=False), "crop_group"] = "urban"
    data["crop_cycles"] = data.MULTIUSE.astype("string").str.strip().map(CYCLES)
    require(data.crop_cycles.notna().all(), f"Unreviewed MULTIUSE values: {path}")
    data["source_fid"] = data.index
    data = data.reset_index(drop=True)
    status = (sorted(data.DataStatus.dropna().astype(str).unique())
              if "DataStatus" in data else ["Not provided for 2020"])
    return data, {"path": str(path), "layer": layer, "crs": str(info["crs"]),
                  "statewide_feature_count_metadata_only": int(info["features"]),
                  "regional_bbox_rows_loaded": len(data), "source_bbox": list(bbox),
                  "regional_data_status": status}

title: Crop mapping — annual agricultural features (2021–2024)
text:
2. Buffer intersections and agricultural features
For every map year, calculate both 500 m and 1,000 m features. Full buffers can cross county boundaries. Crop-group percentages use the theoretical circular area, while mapped-polygon footprint uses the actual buffer area. Unmapped area is not assumed to be nonagricultural land.


Code
def summarize(points, candidates, radius):
    circles = points[["gm_well_id", "geometry"]].copy()
    circles.geometry = circles.buffer(radius, quad_segs=16)
    
    # grouped = candidates.dissolve(by=["crop_group", "crop_cycles"]).reset_index()
    # pieces = gpd.overlay(circles, grouped[["crop_group", "crop_cycles", "geometry"]],
    #                      how="intersection", keep_geom_type=True)
    pieces = gpd.overlay(circles, candidates[["crop_group", "crop_cycles", "geometry"]],
                        how="intersection", keep_geom_type=True)
    
    pieces["area_m2"] = pieces.area
    ids = pd.Index(points.gm_well_id.astype("string"), name="gm_well_id")
    areas = pieces.pivot_table(index="gm_well_id", columns="crop_group",
                               values="area_m2", aggfunc="sum")
    areas = areas.reindex(index=ids, columns=GROUPS, fill_value=0).fillna(0)
    mapped = pieces.groupby("gm_well_id").geometry.apply(lambda s: s.union_all().area)
    mapped = mapped.reindex(ids, fill_value=0)
    summed = areas.sum(axis=1)
    overlap = (summed - mapped).clip(lower=0)
    require(float(overlap.max()) < 1.0, "Mapped classes overlap by >= 1 m2.")
    circle_area = np.pi * radius**2
    buffer_area = pd.Series(circles.area.to_numpy(), index=ids)
    require((mapped <= buffer_area + 1e-4).all(), "Mapped area exceeds buffer.")
    require(np.allclose(buffer_area, circle_area * 0.9983943930356184,
                        rtol=1e-8), "Unexpected buffer units/resolution.")

    table = pd.DataFrame(index=ids)
    for group in GROUPS:
        table[f"pct_{group}_{radius}m"] = areas[group] / circle_area * 100
        # This is composition inside mapped polygons, not a whole-buffer share.
        table[f"pct_{group}_of_mapped_{radius}m"] = (
            areas[group] / mapped.replace(0, np.nan) * 100)
    table[f"pct_cropland_{radius}m"] = areas[FARMED].sum(axis=1) / circle_area * 100
    table[f"pct_cropland_of_mapped_{radius}m"] = (
        areas[FARMED].sum(axis=1) / mapped.replace(0, np.nan) * 100)
    farm = pieces[pieces.crop_group.isin(FARMED)]
    farm_area = farm.groupby("gm_well_id").area_m2.sum().reindex(ids, fill_value=0)
    weighted = (farm.area_m2 * farm.crop_cycles).groupby(farm.gm_well_id).sum()
    table[f"crop_cycles_{radius}m"] = weighted.reindex(ids) / farm_area.replace(0, np.nan)
    multi = farm[farm.crop_cycles.ge(2)].groupby("gm_well_id").area_m2.sum()
    table[f"pct_multicrop_{radius}m"] = multi.reindex(ids, fill_value=0) / circle_area * 100
    table[f"buffer_area_m2_{radius}m"] = buffer_area
    table[f"dwr_polygon_area_m2_{radius}m"] = mapped
    table[f"dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_{radius}m"] = mapped / buffer_area * 100
    table[f"outside_dwr_polygons_pct_{radius}m"] = (
        (buffer_area - mapped).clip(lower=0) / buffer_area * 100)
    table[f"dwr_polygon_status_{radius}m"] = np.where(
        mapped.le(1e-8), "no_dwr_polygon", "dwr_polygon_present_completeness_unknown")
    no_map = mapped.le(1e-8)
    crop_columns = [c for c in table if c.startswith("pct_") or c.startswith("crop_cycles_")]
    table.loc[no_map, crop_columns] = np.nan
    percents = table[[c for c in table if c.startswith("pct_")]]
    require(percents.dropna().ge(-1e-8).all().all()
            and percents.dropna().le(100 + 1e-8).all().all(),
            "Percentage out of bounds.")
    require(table[f"crop_cycles_{radius}m"].dropna().between(1, 4).all(),
            "Crop cycles outside 1-4.")
    qa = {"well_count": len(table), "overlay_piece_count": len(pieces),
          "max_overlap_area_m2": float(overlap.max()),
          "dwr_polygon_status_counts": table[f"dwr_polygon_status_{radius}m"].value_counts().to_dict(),
          "dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_summary": table[f"dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_{radius}m"].describe().to_dict()}
    return table, qa



2.1. Groundwater wells and study area


Code

section: 3. Historical land use and one-year lag
text:
3. Historical land use and one-year lag
For nitrate measurements in 2022–2025, use DWR crop years 2021–2024. Annual changes compare each crop map with the preceding map; 2020 is used only as a baseline for 2021 changes. This is a retrospective modeling assumption, not an estimate of groundwater travel time.


Code
feature_rows, qa_years = [], {}
for year in YEARS:
    measurement_year = year + 1
    wells = obs.loc[obs.measurement_year.eq(measurement_year),
                    ["gm_well_id", "gm_latitude", "gm_longitude"]].drop_duplicates("gm_well_id")
    ids = wells.gm_well_id.astype("string")
    current = map_features[year].loc[ids].copy()
    previous = map_features[year - 1].loc[ids].copy().add_suffix("__previous")
    table = pd.concat([current, previous], axis=1)
    table.insert(0, "gm_well_id", table.index.astype("string"))
    table.insert(1, "crop_year", year)
    table.insert(2, "measurement_year", measurement_year)
    table.insert(3, "dwr_map_status", EXPECTED_STATUS.get(year, "Not provided by source"))
    table.insert(4, "change_base_year", year - 1)
    year_qa = {"measurement_year": measurement_year, "crop_year": year,
               "well_count": len(ids), "rows": len(table),
               "current_map_validation": map_qa[str(year)]}
    for radius in RADII:
        status = (table[f"dwr_polygon_area_m2_{radius}m"].gt(0)
                  & table[f"dwr_polygon_area_m2_{radius}m__previous"].gt(0))
        table[f"annual_change_status_{radius}m"] = np.where(
            status, "both_years_have_polygons_completeness_unknown",
            "no_polygon_in_one_or_both_years")
        for group in [*GROUPS, "cropland", "multicrop"]:
            col = (f"pct_{group}_{radius}m" if group != "multicrop"
                   else f"pct_multicrop_{radius}m")
            delta = f"delta_{group}_pp_{radius}m"
            table[delta] = table[col] - table[f"{col}__previous"]
            table.loc[~status, delta] = np.nan
        col = f"dwr_polygon_footprint_pct_{radius}m"
        table[f"delta_dwr_polygon_footprint_pp_{radius}m"] = (
            table[col] - table[f"{col}__previous"])
        table.loc[~status, f"delta_dwr_polygon_footprint_pp_{radius}m"] = np.nan
    require(table.gm_well_id.is_unique and len(table) == len(ids),
            f"Annual well rows/IDs changed: {year}")
    qa_years[str(year)] = year_qa
    feature_rows.append(table.reset_index(drop=True))
